Hi Sarah — thanks for the details and attachments. Quick answers up front, then I'll follow up with a short checklist you can run in staging.

1) Service hooks: Redwood expects either (a) a JSON body with a top-level "publisher_id" or (b) an HTTP header X-Redwood-Publisher: <publisher_id>. Microsoft sometimes strips custom headers in their intermediary router; if you see 200s but missing fields, switch to including publisher_id in the payload body under event.metadata.publisher_id.

2) SKU mapping: our recommended pattern is to use the offer manifest's "plan" id as the stable mapping key (not the display name). In the ARM payload, ensure the plan id is the machine-readable token (e.g., acme.starter.v1). That token should be echoed back on entitlement callbacks as offerId/planId — we map that directly to the license SKU on our side.

Checklist for your staging run:
- Confirm webhook receives event.type = "EntitlementActivated" and event.metadata.publisher_id present
- Confirm callback contains offer.planId (example: acme.starter.v1)
- Run entitlement ping from Azure sandbox and verify TTL header TTL-Window is present

I'll ask Karthik to paste a minimal manifest snippet and a short script you can run that validates the mapping locally. We're able to join a quick screen-share if you want to run this together.

Regards,

Hi Sarah — sharing a minimal manifest/ARM mapping and a tiny validation curl you can run in the staging subscription. Paste this into a file called manifest-snippet.json and replace <PUBLISHER_ID> and <PLAN_TOKEN>.

--- manifest-snippet.json (excerpt) ---
{
  "name": "acme-cloud-saas",
  "plans": [
    {"id": "acme.starter.v1", "display": "Starter"},
    {"id": "acme.scale.v1", "display": "Scale"},
    {"id": "acme.enterprise.v1", "display": "Enterprise"}
  ]
}

Sample entitlement callback expectation (payload we will receive from MS):
{
  "eventType": "EntitlementActivated",
  "offer": {"id":"<OFFER_ID>", "planId":"acme.starter.v1"},
  "metadata": {"publisher_id":"<PUBLISHER_ID>", "tenant":"<TENANT_ID>"}
}

Quick validation curl (replace variables):
curl -X POST https://staging-hooks.acmecloud.com/azhook -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '@test-payload.json' -v

If the callback is missing publisher_id, include it as a header: -H "X-Redwood-Publisher: <PUBLISHER_ID>"

I'll also attach a lightweight Node script we use internally to assert planId -> SKU mapping; happy to drop into your repo.

-Karthik

Hi Sarah — quick answer on precedence and a plan for validation tomorrow:

Precedence we apply on Redwood systems: 1) planId (if present) -> guaranteed canonical mapping, 2) planName -> normalized and matched case-insensitively against manifest display names, 3) fallback to SKU alias in the Azure offer metadata if neither present (least reliable).

Action plan:
- We'll update our ingress to accept planName as a fallback and normalize known aliases from your spreadsheet (we imported the matrix you attached).
- Marcus and I will run a sandbox activation from our side against your staging hooks at 10:00 AM PDT tomorrow and share the full capture/logs.
- If planId is absent in MS callbacks, we'll follow up with step-by-step guidance on setting the "plan ID" field in the Offer creation UI (it's in the Plans -> Advanced settings, small "internal id" field) and an ARM snippet to inject it during offer provisioning.
